notes: Clicked for credits for many turns while sitting on 20-37 credits and never built a breaker suite, so it let the Corp advance and score two Fujii in remotes almost uncontested. At the end it idled at 22-30 credits while the Corp set up and scored the winning point.

Solid scoring plan behind Unsmiling Tsarevna and decent tag pressure, but it repeatedly took Tsarevna's optional draws into a full hand (discarding 5 at once). It also installed Tomorrow's Headline behind ice with no end-the-run subroutine, and the Runner stole it.

Sat at 0 credits for about 20 turns and spent every click re-running R&D and HQ, repeatedly hitting Behold!, ending turns heavily tagged and eating End of the Line. It saw Bellona many times and never got the 5 credits to steal it; the win came only because the Corp decked.

Lost an early agenda to Inside Job, then scored three agendas in well-iced remotes and used Weyland advancement economy sensibly. It was slow to push agendas in the middle turns while holding plenty of credits.

Against an NBN tag deck it kept running through tagging ice, used a Trick Shot follow-up to facecheck an empty remote (Tsarevna net damage), and ended the turn with several tags and 3 cards. End of the Line then flatlined it.

Never built a scoring remote and kept Bellonas and False Lead in an HQ behind one Ping, which the Runner raided for the win. It clicked for credits while rich with a full hand and spent whole turns on repeated useless attempts to trash DJ Fenris.

Spent many turns on convoluted setup (The Price, Gachapon, Bling, Ashen Epilogue) and Archives runs instead of pressuring HQ and R&D while the Corp was passive. It eventually assembled breaking and won with a strong final turn.

Clicked for credits up to 38 for nine turns while the Corp scored two Regenesis from barely iced remotes. Later it bounced off a rezzed Tatu-Bola more than 20 times with no way to break it while the Corp advanced and scored behind it.

Never installed an agenda, clicked for credits for many turns, and left Bellonas and False Lead in an HQ behind one Ping for the Runner to steal. It burned whole turns on repeated attempts to trash the same resource.

Clean Weyland game: an early iced remote score, NGO Front and Government Subsidy economy, and layered ice (Border Control, Pharos) to close out three agendas. Its only oddities were a few minor idle clicks.
Efficient fast-advance from a single iced remote, scoring out by turn 11 with Bladderwort pings. It left R&D unprotected all game against a Runner running it four times a turn, which was risky.

Stayed tagged at low credits against NBN and lost four cards to End of the Line. For roughly ten turns it barely ran HQ, which had one Ping, while the Corp hoarded credits, and it won late mainly off Archives and HQ accesses.

Installed only one ice and never iced R&D or Archives against a sabotage Runner, who stole agendas from Archives and HQ. It spent nearly every click gaining credits or drawing and played Shipment from Vladisibirsk to no effect.

Stayed at 0 credits all game, ran R&D four times a turn into Behold! and Virtual Service Agent, collected huge tag counts, and took two End of the Line hits. It also re-ran a known advanced Chekist Scion for 11 tags; the win came only from Corp decking.

After a strong turn-1 steal it mostly clicked for credits and ran Archives while the Corp advanced and scored three agendas in its main remote. It declined to steal the winning Send a Message when Pinhole Threading reached it.
Installed no ice on R&D or Archives against a sabotage and multi-access Runner and spent turns clicking for credits and drawing. It played IP Enforcement to no effect and lost on turn 4.

Kept reasonable HQ pressure with Unity and Diversion of Funds, but it had no barrier answer early and let two agendas score from the remote. Its late remote run spent all its credits on Pharos and lost Curupira to Winchester.

It clicked for credits for several turns while rich and discarding, but once it started it steadily scored small agendas behind Tatu-Bola and baited the Runner with a Snare. It won comfortably against a passive Runner.
Coherent net-damage plan: it scored behind Semak-samun, stacked Bladderworts, and used Anemone and See How They Run to strip the grip for a turn-7 flatline. Its credits ran very thin at times.
Correctly hammered an unprotected R&D with every click and won on turn 4. Going to 0 credits on turn 1 was loose but cost nothing here.
